planting.note: Plant container-grown plants or rooted cuttings in spring in poor to average, sharply drained soil in a full-sun, sheltered position; Green Ginger is an RHS Award of Garden Merit selection valued for its unusually cold-hardy constitution and distinctive ginger-scented foliage.

directions: Green Ginger is a bushy, upright rosemary cultivar with narrow, dark green needle-like leaves that release a distinctive ginger note alongside the typical resinous rosemary scent when crushed, making it a novelty choice for cooks who want a warmer, spicier undertone in rosemary dishes. It bears clusters of pale blue-and-white, two-lipped flowers in the leaf axils from mid-spring through summer, often repeating sporadically into autumn. Among the hardiest rosemary selections available, it tolerates winter cold well below what damages many other cultivars and has earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for garden-worthiness. Grow it in poor to average, sharply drained soil in a sunny, sheltered spot; like all rosemary it resents heavy, wet soil far more than it minds cold, so drainage is the key to long-term success.

common_name: Santa Cruz Oregano (Trailing Ornamental Hop-Flowered Oregano)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants after the last hard frost in lean, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Santa Cruz is a vigorous, drought-tolerant ornamental oregano grown chiefly for its trailing habit and papery pink-flushed flower bracts rather than for culinary use.

directions: Santa Cruz is a vigorous, spreading ornamental oregano selected for its showy, hop-like flower clusters rather than kitchen use, since its small upright foliage carries very little of the typical oregano fragrance. Violet, trumpet-shaped flowers with pink overtones and lime-green calyces appear at the stem tips from midsummer through fall, tumbling attractively over rocks, walls, and slopes, and holding their color well when cut and dried for wreaths and arrangements. It tolerates heat and drought once established, making it a good choice for a low-water border or xeriscape planting. Grow in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade with moderate to occasional watering, and shear back after flowering to keep growth dense and tidy.
